subject.title: [Feature] Decouple dreaming from memory-core — allow any memory plugin to implement dreaming protocol

question: Should OpenClaw core own a public dreaming provider protocol and scheduler contract for memory plugins, or should dreaming orchestration remain plugin-owned through ClawHub packages?
rationale: The request crosses public plugin SDK, config, scheduling, memory state, and upgrade boundaries, and the existing ClawHub workaround does not determine whether core should add a new extension point.

options.title: Design Core SDK Protocol
options.body: Accept the feature direction by specifying a minimal dreaming provider capability, scheduler ownership, config shape, and compatibility path, preferably after reconciling #88504's memory role-slot work.

options.title: Keep Dreaming Plugin-Owned
options.body: Close or narrow this issue by documenting ClawHub plugins as the supported path and declining a core-managed dreaming scheduler protocol for now.

options.title: Defer Behind Role Slots
options.body: Keep this issue blocked until memory role slots land, then revisit whether memory.dreaming needs a runtime provider contract beyond slot selection.

recommendation.title: Design Core SDK Protocol
recommendation.body: Accept the feature direction by specifying a minimal dreaming provider capability, scheduler ownership, config shape, and compatibility path, preferably after reconciling #88504's memory role-slot work.

likelyOwner.reason: The open choice is product/API direction for a memory-core-to-plugin SDK boundary, and recent history shows steipete carrying adjacent dreaming architecture work.
